THE TOOL FOR THIS WHOLE UNIT
Every claim in Decks 21 to 24 gets one of these four labels.
Tested many ways by many teams. It could still change, but only with big new evidence.
Testable, with some evidence for it, but not confirmed. Scientists still argue about it.
e.g. inflation; dark energy may change over time
Fits known physics, but has little or no evidence yet. Often very hard to test today.
e.g. wormholes you could travel through
Nobody knows yet, or the evidence is disputed.
e.g. what dark matter is made of
A wild idea can still be science, if it passes these three checks.
It makes a prediction you could check with an observation or experiment.
Some result could prove it wrong. If nothing could ever prove it wrong, it is not science.
Experts review the methods before it is published, and other teams try to repeat it.
Something we cannot see is pulling on everything we can.
How do you weigh something invisible?
Vera Rubin & Kent Ford measure how fast Andromeda's stars orbit
Stars far from a galaxy's center orbit about as fast as stars near the center.
The visible stars and gas do not have enough gravity to hold those fast outer stars.
So something extra is pulling: unseen mass, or gravity that works differently.
MASS BENDS LIGHT: THE BULLET CLUSTER
mass bends the light from objects behind it, like a giant lens
Einstein's general relativity predicted light bending; the 1919 solar eclipse measured it.
In the Bullet Cluster, two galaxy clusters collided. Lensing shows most mass is offset from the hot gas.
Best explanation: dark matter passed straight through the crash while the gas slowed down.
ABOUT 5 TIMES MORE DARK MATTER THAN ATOMS
dark matter vs. ordinary matter, share of the universe (Planck 2018)
Planck mapped tiny hot and cold spots in the cosmic microwave background (Deck 19).
The spot pattern fits only if there is about 5 times more dark matter than ordinary matter.
Dark matter does not give off, absorb or reflect light. We see only its gravity.
Many teams are hunting. Nobody has caught dark matter yet.
• gravity changes when pulls are very weak
• fits many galaxy rotation curves well

Something is making the universe's expansion speed up.
If gravity pulls everything together, why is expansion getting faster?
Hubble: distant galaxies move away. The universe is expanding.
Two teams: far-away Type Ia supernovae are dimmer than expected.
Nobel Prize to Perlmutter, Schmidt & Riess for the speed-up.
DESI maps 14 million galaxies: hints that dark energy changes.
'Dark energy' is the name for whatever causes the speed-up. What it is:
Dark energy is about 68% of the universe's energy (Planck 2018).
The universe expands forever. Stars burn out. Everything gets cold and dark.
Dark energy grows stronger and tears apart galaxies, then stars, then atoms.
The expansion stops and reverses. Everything falls back together.

What do we actually know about black holes, and what are we guessing?
2015: LIGO detects gravitational waves from two black holes merging.
2019: the Event Horizon Telescope images the shadow of M87*. 2022: Sgr A*, at our galaxy's center.
Hawking radiation: black holes should slowly leak energy (Hawking, 1974). Never observed.
What happens at the very center (the singularity)?
a tunnel through spacetime that would link two far-apart places
Einstein's equations allow wormhole solutions on paper.
Keeping one open would need 'exotic' matter with negative energy (Morris & Thorne, 1988).
No wormhole has ever been observed.
